description:
Hit by three example authors today (monte_carlo_rtp.exs, geohash_crc.exs, and the guidance trio): an `if`/`cond`/`case` whose arms are tuples is rejected with branch-tuple, so an author writes one if per element. The rewrite is mechanical and the compiler can do it: lower a tuple-valued branch as one branch per element position (each element's arms are the corresponding elements of the tuple arms, with the condition evaluated once into a temporary; selects apply per element when the arms are pure), binding the result as a tuple value `%{elems: ...}` like a reduce accumulator does. Elixir mode: the tuple branch is plain Elixir already. Arrays inside such tuples stay rejected until defk-gqk (arrays through branches).

Tests: both modes via assert_agrees for if, cond and case with 2- and 3-tuples, mixed i64/f64 elements (type-checked per position), a select check on the generated C for pure arms, and the array-in-tuple rejection. Docs: section 7 of docs/language.md; retire or re-word the branch-tuple code (grep docs/language.md for links to it).

Done when: the three examples' per-element ifs can be written as one tuple branch (update at least one), agreement holds, suite green.

comments.text: Decisions: (1) branch-tuple code kept (codes are never renamed) but re-worded and re-kinded :subset -> :error: it now means arms that are not all tuples of the same size. (2) Tuple arms lower to ONE if/else chain assigning every element temp (conditions run once), or, when all arms are pure, one select per element over shared cond temps with a single overflow flag and replay. (3) Per-position types via branch_type!/4 (branch-types message names the element, 1-based; array element -> array-in-branch). (4) Bitstring elements supported the same way bitstring branches are (bits_arms per position; <<>> beside a bitstring arm is the empty bitstring), tested. (5) Examples: geohash_crc decode and sort_u64_keys use one tuple branch; monte_carlo_rtp and the other guidance scripts had no per-element kernel ifs left on main.

title: Tuples from if/cond/case: {a, b} = if c, do: {x, y}, else: {u, v}
